subject: Chemistry
source_note: Compiled from the NTA JEE Main 2026 Information Bulletin / official syllabus as reported by multiple 2025-2026 coaching/exam-tracker sources (careers360, shiksha, giraffe-learning), cross-checked Sep 2026. Several chapters were removed in the 2024-25 rationalisation (Surface Chemistry, States of Matter, s-Block Elements, Hydrogen, Environmental Chemistry, Polymers, Chemistry in Everyday Life, General Principles of Isolation of Metals). Always verify against the current-year NTA information bulletin (jeemain.nta.nic.in) before finalising a question bank, since NTA can revise the syllabus PDF between sessions.
exam_pattern_note: JEE Main Paper 1 Chemistry: 25 questions total (Section A: 20 single-correct MCQs, Section B: 5 numerical-value questions, all 25 compulsory since the 2025 pattern change removed the earlier 'attempt any 5 of 10' choice in Section B). No multiple-correct or matrix-match question types appear in JEE Main (those are JEE-Advanced-only formats).

subtopics: Matter and its nature, Dalton's atomic theory; atom, molecule, element, compound
Laws of chemical combination
Atomic and molecular masses, mole concept, molar mass, percentage composition
Empirical and molecular formulae
Chemical equations and stoichiometry
topics.syllabus_change_note: 2025 rationalisation dropped 'physical quantities and their measurement in Chemistry, precision and accuracy, significant figures, SI units, dimensional analysis' as a separately examinable line item from this unit.

subtopics: Electromagnetic radiation, photoelectric effect, hydrogen spectrum
Bohr model of the hydrogen atom: postulates, energy/radii derivations, limitations
Dual nature of matter, de Broglie relation, Heisenberg uncertainty principle
Quantum mechanical model of the atom, atomic orbitals, Ψ and Ψ² for 1s/2s
Quantum numbers, shapes of s/p/d orbitals, electron spin
Aufbau principle, Pauli exclusion principle, Hund's rule, electronic configuration and extra stability of half-filled/filled orbitals
Kossel-Lewis approach, ionic and covalent bonds
Ionic bonding: formation, factors, lattice enthalpy
Covalent bonding: electronegativity, Fajan's rule, dipole moment, VSEPR theory and molecular shapes
Valence bond theory, hybridisation (s, p, d), resonance
Molecular orbital theory: LCAO, bonding/antibonding MOs, sigma/pi bonds, bond order, bond length, bond energy
Metallic bonding, hydrogen bonding and applications
System/surroundings, extensive/intensive properties, state functions, entropy, types of processes
First law: work, heat, internal energy, enthalpy, heat capacity, Hess's law
Enthalpies of bond dissociation, combustion, formation, atomisation, sublimation, phase transition, hydration, ionisation, solution
Second law: spontaneity, ΔS(universe) and ΔG(system) as criteria for spontaneity
ΔG° and equilibrium constant
topics.syllabus_change_note: 2025 rationalisation trimmed a standalone Carnot-engine-style efficiency treatment; the ΔG-spontaneity and Hess's-law content remain fully examinable.

subtopics: Concentration expressions: molality, molarity, mole fraction, percentage
Vapour pressure of solutions, Raoult's law, ideal and non-ideal solutions
Colligative properties: relative lowering of vapour pressure, depression of freezing point, elevation of boiling point, osmotic pressure
Determination of molecular mass using colligative properties, abnormal molar mass, van't Hoff factor
Concept of dynamic equilibrium
Physical equilibria: solid-liquid, liquid-gas, gas-gas, solid-gas, Henry's law
Ionic equilibrium: weak/strong electrolytes, Arrhenius/Bronsted-Lowry/Lewis acid-base concepts
Acid-base equilibria including multistage ionisation, ionisation constants, ionisation of water, pH scale
Common ion effect, salt hydrolysis and pH, solubility product, buffer solutions
Oxidation and reduction: electronic concept, oxidation number, balancing redox reactions
Electrolytic and metallic conduction, molar conductivity and variation with concentration, Kohlrausch's law
Electrolytic and Galvanic cells, electrode potential, standard electrode potential
EMF of a Galvanic cell, Nernst equation, relation between cell potential and Gibbs energy change
Dry cell, lead accumulator, fuel cells
Rate of a reaction, factors affecting rate: concentration, temperature, pressure, catalyst
Elementary/complex reactions, order and molecularity
Rate law, rate constant and units
Differential and integral forms of zero- and first-order reactions, half-lives
Effect of temperature: Arrhenius theory, activation energy
Collision theory of bimolecular gaseous reactions (no derivation)

topics.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
subtopics: Modern periodic law, present form of the periodic table
s, p, d, f block elements
Periodic trends: atomic/ionic radii, ionisation enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy, valence, oxidation states, chemical reactivity
Group 13-18 general trends: electronic configuration, physical/chemical property trends, anomalous first-element behaviour
Group 13: boron, aluminium, borax, boric acid, diborane, BF3, AlCl3, alums
Group 14: catenation, allotropes/oxides of carbon, silicates, zeolites, silicones
Group 15: nitrogen, phosphorus, ammonia, nitric acid, phosphine, phosphorus halides, oxides/oxoacids of N and P
Group 16: ozone, sulphur allotropes, sulphuric acid, oxoacids of sulphur
Group 17: hydrochloric acid, acidic strength of hydrogen halides, interhalogens, oxides/oxoacids of halogens
Group 18: noble gases, fluorides and oxides of xenon
Transition elements: general introduction, electronic configuration, occurrence, characteristics

Trends in first-row transition elements: physical properties, ionisation enthalpy, oxidation states, atomic radii, colour, catalytic behaviour, magnetic properties, complex formation, interstitial compounds, alloys
Preparation, properties, uses of K2Cr2O7 and KMnO4
Lanthanoids: electronic configuration, oxidation states, lanthanoid contraction
Actinoids: electronic configuration and oxidation states
Werner's theory, ligands, coordination number, denticity, chelation
IUPAC nomenclature of mononuclear coordination compounds, isomerism
Bonding: valence bond approach, basic ideas of crystal field theory, colour and magnetic properties
Importance of coordination compounds in qualitative analysis, metal extraction, biological systems

topics.chapter: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
subtopics: Purification: crystallisation, sublimation, distillation, differential extraction, chromatography
Qualitative analysis: detection of nitrogen, sulphur, phosphorus, halogens
Quantitative analysis (basic principles): estimation of C, H, N, halogens, sulphur, phosphorus
Calculation of empirical and molecular formulae

topics.chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
subtopics: Tetravalency of carbon, hybridisation, classification by functional groups, homologous series
Isomerism: structural and stereoisomerism, IUPAC nomenclature
Covalent bond fission: homolytic/heterolytic, free radicals, carbocations, carbanions, stability
Electrophiles and nucleophiles
Electronic displacement: inductive effect, electromeric effect, resonance, hyperconjugation
Common reaction types: substitution, addition, elimination, rearrangement
Classification, isomerism, IUPAC nomenclature, general preparation/properties/reactions
Alkanes: conformations (Sawhorse, Newman for ethane), mechanism of halogenation
Alkenes: geometrical isomerism, electrophilic addition mechanism, Markovnikov/peroxide effect, ozonolysis, polymerisation
Alkynes: acidic character, addition reactions, polymerisation
Aromatic hydrocarbons: benzene structure and aromaticity, electrophilic substitution mechanism, halogenation, nitration, Friedel-Crafts alkylation/acylation, directive influence of substituents
General methods of preparation, properties, reactions
Nature of the C-X bond, mechanisms of substitution reactions
Uses and environmental effects of chloroform, iodoform, freons, DDT
Alcohols: identification of 1°/2°/3° alcohols, mechanism of dehydration
Phenols: acidic nature, electrophilic substitution, halogenation, nitration, sulphonation, Reimer-Tiemann reaction
Ethers: structure

Aldehydes and ketones: nucleophilic addition, Grignard reagent, oxidation, reduction (Wolff-Kishner, Clemmensen), acidity of α-hydrogen, aldol condensation, Cannizzaro reaction, haloform reaction, distinguishing tests
Carboxylic acids: acidic strength and factors affecting it
General methods of preparation, properties, reactions, uses
Amines: nomenclature, classification, structure, basic character, identification of 1°/2°/3° amines
Diazonium salts: importance in synthetic organic chemistry
General introduction and importance of biomolecules
Carbohydrates: aldoses/ketoses, monosaccharides (glucose, fructose), constituent monosaccharides of sucrose/lactose/maltose
Proteins: α-amino acids, peptide bond, polypeptides, primary/secondary/tertiary/quaternary structure (qualitative), denaturation, enzymes
Vitamins: classification and functions
Nucleic acids: chemical constitution of DNA and RNA, biological functions
Detection of extra elements (N, S, halogens) and functional groups (hydroxyl, carbonyl, carboxyl, amino) in organic compounds
Chemistry of preparation: Mohr's salt, potash alum (inorganic); acetanilide, p-nitroacetanilide, aniline yellow, iodoform (organic)
Titrimetric exercises: acid-base with indicators, oxalic acid vs KMnO4, Mohr's salt vs KMnO4
Qualitative salt analysis: cations (Pb2+, Cu2+, Al3+, Fe3+, Zn2+, Ni2+, Ca2+, Ba2+, Mg2+, NH4+), anions (CO3^2-, S^2-, SO4^2-, NO3-, NO2-, Cl-, Br-, I-); insoluble salts excluded
Chemical principles of experiments: enthalpy of solution of CuSO4, enthalpy of neutralisation, preparation of lyophilic/lyophobic sols, kinetics of iodide-hydrogen peroxide reaction
